function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here are a few ways you can order a cake, depending on whether you’re looking for something local or something that can be delivered right to your doorstep: | Option | What it offers | How to order | |--------|----------------|--------------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; you can visit in person or call. | Search “bakery near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, then call or visit the shop. | | **National cake delivery chains** | Nationwide coverage, consistent quality, sometimes same‑day delivery. |
• **Goldbelly** – delivers specialty cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S.
• **Cake Delivery** – local delivery in many cities.
• **Baker’s Dozen** – custom cakes delivered to your address. | | **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety of styles, often user reviews, and easy comparison. |
• **Etsy** – find local artisans who ship nationwide.
• **Amazon** – some sellers offer fresh cakes that can be refrigerated. | | **Specialty dessert shops** | Gourmet, themed, or dietary‑specific cakes (gluten‑free, vegan, keto). |
• **The Cake Shop** – specializes in vegan and gluten‑free options.
• **Cakes & Bites** – offers custom designs for events. | | **Subscription services** | Monthly cake deliveries for birthdays, anniversaries, or just for fun. |
• **Cake Club** – delivers a new cake each month.
• **Sweet Treats Subscription** – offers seasonal flavors. | ### Quick steps to place an order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** (birthday, wedding, custom design, dietary restrictions). 2. **Choose a provider** from the table above that fits your location and budget. 3. **Visit their website or call** to place your order. Most sites let you: - Pick a flavor and size - Add decorations or custom messages - Schedule a delivery date/time 4. **Confirm payment** (credit card, PayPal, or sometimes cash on delivery). 5. **Track the order** if the service offers tracking or delivery notifications. #### Example: Ordering a birthday cake from Goldbelly 1. Go to [goldbelly.com](https://www.goldbelly.com). 2. Search “birthday cake” or browse the “Birthday Cakes” category. 3. Select a cake you like (e.g., “Chocolate Lava Cake” from a renowned bakery). 4. Click “Add to Cart,” choose the delivery date, and enter your address. 5. Checkout with your payment details. 6. You’ll receive a confirmation email and a delivery estimate. If you let me know your city or any specific preferences (like vegan, gluten‑free, or a particular flavor), I can narrow down the best options for you!
